title: Microsoft Purview eDiscovery: who can search, hold and delete organisational content, and what it costs
summary: Hold: the hold-policy API creates a policy but does not select the mailboxes or sites the row says it preserves. The page also incorrectly implies that eDiscovery permissions require a mail-enabled security group, although Microsoft documents assigning individual users.

claims.claim: Purview eDiscovery identifies and delivers electronic information as evidence in investigations and legal cases.
claims.quote: Electronic discovery, or eDiscovery, is the process of identifying and delivering electronically stored information (ESI) that you can use as evidence in investigations and legal cases.

claims.claim: A case contains the searches, holds and review sets for an investigation.
claims.quote: An eDiscovery case contains all searches, holds, and review sets related to a specific investigation.

claims.where: What it is, first paragraph; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: Case membership controls access to the case and its contents.
claims.quote: You can also assign members to a case to control who can access the case and view the contents of the case.

claims.claim: Search supports Exchange, OneDrive, SharePoint, Teams, Microsoft 365 Groups and Viva Engage.
claims.quote: Search for content that's stored in Exchange mailboxes, OneDrive accounts, SharePoint sites, Microsoft Teams, Microsoft 365 Groups, and Viva Engage Teams.

claims.claim: One eDiscovery search can search mailboxes and sites together.
claims.quote: You can search mailboxes and sites in the same eDiscovery search, and then export the search results.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot interactions are individual items in the user's Exchange Online mailbox.
claims.quote: Each Microsoft 365 Copilot interaction is stored in the user's Exchange Online mailbox as an individual message-class item

claims.where: summary; What it is, second paragraph
claims.claim: Copilot interaction data can be searched, preserved and exported with eDiscovery.
claims.quote: eDiscovery content search, legal hold, export search results for Copilot interactions

claims.claim: Microsoft retired classic eDiscovery experiences on 31 August 2025.
claims.quote: Microsoft retired all classic eDiscovery experiences on August 31, 2025.

claims.claim: The current experience is eDiscovery in the Microsoft Purview portal.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft Purview portal, all Content Search functionality is now included in a system generated eDiscovery case

claims.where: What it is, The parts: Search
claims.claim: Search finds content using keyword queries and conditions.
claims.quote: Create Keyword Query Language (KeyQL) search queries to search for content keywords that match query criteria. You can also include conditions to narrow the scope of your search.

claims.where: What it is, The parts: Search
claims.claim: Search provides statistics and samples.
claims.quote: You can also view a representative sample of the items included in the search results.

claims.where: What it is, The parts: Hold; Why it matters
claims.claim: Case holds preserve selected mailbox and site content until the location is removed or the hold is released.
claims.quote: When you place content locations on hold, you preserve content until you remove the content location from the hold or until you delete or release the hold.

claims.where: What it is, The parts: Export
claims.claim: Export copies results from their original locations into a downloadable package.
claims.quote: When you export search results, items are copied from their original content location and packaged. Then you can download those items in the export package to a local computer.

claims.where: What it is, The parts: Review set
claims.claim: A review set is a Microsoft-provided Azure Storage copy of collected items.
claims.quote: A review set is a secure, Microsoft-provided Azure Storage location in the Microsoft cloud. When you add data to a review set, the collected items are copied from their original content location to the review set.

claims.where: What it is, The parts: Review set
claims.claim: Review sets support filtering, tagging and analysis.
claims.quote: Review sets provide a static, known set of content that you can search, filter, tag, analyze, and predict relevancy using predictive coding models.

claims.where: What it is, The parts: Search and delete
claims.claim: Search and delete can remove harmful or high-risk email, Teams messages and Copilot or AI application data.
claims.quote: Use eDiscovery to search for and delete email messages, Microsoft Teams chat messages, and Copilot and AI application data across your organization. This capability helps you find and remove content that's potentially harmful or high-risk.

claims.claim: Review sets, analytics, tagging and decryption are premium rather than standard features.
claims.quote:
| Review sets |  | ![Supported.](media/check-mark.png) |
| Decryption |  | ![Supported.](media/check-mark.png) |
| Tagging |  | ![Supported.](media/check-mark.png) |
| Analytics |  | ![Supported.](media/check-mark.png) |

claims.where: What it is, final paragraph; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: Role-based permissions determine which eDiscovery tasks users can perform.
claims.quote: Use role-based access control (RBAC) permissions to control what eDiscovery-related tasks that different users can perform.

claims.claim: Search permissions filters build compliance boundaries limiting the mailboxes and sites a manager can search.
claims.quote: Use search permissions filtering to create logical boundaries (called compliance boundaries) within an organization that control the user content locations (such as mailboxes, SharePoint sites, and OneDrive accounts) that specific eDiscovery managers can search.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends retention policies and labels for long-term retention unrelated to investigations.
claims.quote: For long term data retention not related to eDiscovery investigations, use retention policies and retention labels.

claims.claim: eDiscovery covers content generated by other applications when that content is stored in mailboxes and sites.
claims.quote: Searches include content generated by other Microsoft 365 apps that store data in mailboxes and sites.

claims.claim: The documented Microsoft 365 Copilot item class is IPM.SkypeTeams.Message.Copilot.*.
claims.quote: | Microsoft 365 Copilot | `IPM.SkypeTeams.Message.Copilot.*` |

claims.claim: Standard eDiscovery for sites and files is Included in all columns of the cited service-description table, including the E3 column.
claims.quote: | eDiscovery (standard) for sites and files | Included | Included | Included | Included | Included |

claims.claim: Standard eDiscovery for email is Included in all columns of that table, including the E3 column.
claims.quote: | eDiscovery (standard) for email | Included | Included | Included | Included | Included |

claims.claim: Premium is Included in the table's E5, Purview Suite and eDiscovery & Audit add-on columns, and Not included in its E3 columns.
claims.quote: | eDiscovery (premium) | Included | Not included | Included | Included | Not included |

claims.claim: Compliance boundaries have no separate licensing requirement beyond applicable eDiscovery licensing.
claims.quote: Compliance boundaries are an eDiscovery configuration capability for limiting which content locations and cases eDiscovery managers can access, and don't have separate licensing requirements beyond applicable eDiscovery licensing.

claims.where: Cost and licensing, Holds; What to check
claims.claim: Every user whose content is preserved by a hold needs an eligible licence.
claims.quote: eDiscovery holds require an eligible license on every user whose content you preserve.

claims.claim: Office 365 F1 and F3 do not include rights to be the target of an eDiscovery hold.
claims.quote: Frontline subscriptions such as Office 365 F1 and F3 don't include the rights required to be the target of an eDiscovery hold.

claims.claim: A shared mailbox on hold needs Exchange Online Plan 2 or Plan 1 with Exchange Online Archiving.
claims.quote: Placing a shared mailbox on hold using Microsoft Purview eDiscovery (standard or premium) is subject to the same licensing requirements as placing a hold directly in Exchange Online—Exchange Online Plan 2 or Exchange Online Plan 1 with the Exchange Online Archiving add‑on.

claims.claim: The permissions page requires E5 or an eligible add-on for the user whose data is analysed.
claims.quote: To analyze a user's data when premium eDiscovery features are enabled, the user must be assigned an Office 365 E5 or Microsoft 365 E5 license.

claims.where: Cost and licensing, Premium analysis; Open questions
claims.claim: The permissions page says administrators assigned to cases do not need E5.
claims.quote: Administrators, compliance officers, or legal personnel who are assigned to cases as members and use premium eDiscovery features to collect, view, and analyze data don't need an E5 license.

claims.where: Cost and licensing, Premium analysis; Open questions
claims.claim: The service description instead requires the appropriate licence or add-on for both the analysed user and the administrator.
claims.quote: When eDiscovery (premium) features are used, both the user whose data is being analyzed and the administrator performing the analysis must have the appropriate license or add-on.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 non-AI data storage is included in the enterprise subscription.
claims.quote: This data storage is included in your enterprise subscription and isn't subject to pay-as-you-go billing.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 AI data storage is included rather than billed pay-as-you-go.
claims.quote: This data storage is included in your enterprise subscription and isn't subject to pay-as-you-go billing.

claims.claim: Non-Microsoft 365 AI data storage is subject to pay-as-you-go billing.
claims.quote: This data storage isn't included in your enterprise subscription and is subject to pay-as-you-go billing.

claims.claim: The non-Microsoft 365 AI billing category includes Fabric Copilot, Security Copilot and connected or cloud AI applications.
claims.quote: This data type includes Copilot in Microsoft Fabric, Microsoft Security Copilot, and any connected or cloud AI application.

claims.claim: Direct portal export of non-Microsoft 365 AI data is a billable process.
claims.quote:
The following eDiscovery processes use pay-as-you-go billing for non-Microsoft 365 AI data:

- Direct export of this data from cases by using the Microsoft Purview portal

claims.claim: Adding non-Microsoft 365 AI data to a review set is a billable process.
claims.quote:
The following eDiscovery processes use pay-as-you-go billing for non-Microsoft 365 AI data:

- Direct export of this data from cases by using the Microsoft Purview portal
- Adding this data to a review set

claims.claim: Exporting non-Microsoft 365 AI data through Graph is a billable process.
claims.quote:
The following eDiscovery processes use pay-as-you-go billing for non-Microsoft 365 AI data:

- Direct export of this data from cases by using the Microsoft Purview portal
- Adding this data to a review set
- Exporting this data by using Microsoft Graph API

claims.claim: Search, hold and case-management processes do not incur the non-Microsoft 365 AI data pay-as-you-go charges.
claims.quote:
The following eDiscovery processes don't use pay-as-you-go billing for non-Microsoft 365 AI data and are included in your enterprise subscription:

- All search processes
- All hold processes
- All case management processes

claims.claim: Microsoft publishes the per-GB eDiscovery storage rate on the Purview pricing page rather than the billing article.
claims.quote: This functionality is billed based on the amount of data processed and stored through export and review set each month, equivalent to $20 per GB per month.

claims.claim: Graph API use with E3 eDiscovery licences requires an Azure subscription configured for pay-as-you-go.
claims.quote: Before you can use features associated with non-Microsoft 365 AI data in eDiscovery in your organization, or use Microsoft Graph APIs with an E3 eDiscovery license, you must configure an Azure subscription for pay-as-you-go billing.

claims.claim: Currently all APIs except Export APIs do not contribute towards E3 API billing.
claims.quote: Currently, usage of all APIs except Export APIs doesn't contribute towards billing.

claims.claim: Export API billing is volume-based above an included monthly free amount.
claims.quote: Usage of Export API is billed based on the volume of data exported. Each organization receives an included amount of free storage per month, with additional usage billed at a set price per GB.

claims.where: Risks and limits, eDiscovery Administrators; Governance controls: Roles
claims.claim: eDiscovery Administrators can access all cases and case data, and add themselves to any case to manage it.
claims.quote:
Access case data for any case in the organization.
    - Manage any eDiscovery case after they add themselves as a member of the case.

claims.where: Risks and limits, eDiscovery Administrators; What to check
claims.claim: Microsoft advises limiting the number of eDiscovery Administrators.
claims.quote: because eDiscovery Administrators can access potentially sensitive information in the results of a compliance search, you should limit the number of people who are eDiscovery Administrators.

claims.where: Risks and limits, eDiscovery Administrators; Governance controls: Roles
claims.claim: An eDiscovery Manager can access and manage only cases they create.
claims.quote: eDiscovery Managers can only access and manage the cases they create. They can't access or manage cases created by other eDiscovery Managers.
claims.fix: Replace the unqualified creator-only statements with 'The permissions page describes Managers as limited to cases they create, while the service description and case-access guidance say Managers can access cases of which they are members.' The latter guidance is at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/edisc-settings-access-permissions and the already-cited Purview service description.

claims.where: Risks and limits, A case can lock itself; What to check
claims.claim: If a case's sole member leaves, an eDiscovery Administrator can recover access by adding a member.
claims.quote: because an eDiscovery Administrator can access all eDiscovery cases in the organization, they can view the case and add themselves or another eDiscovery manager as a member of the case.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risks and limits, A case can lock itself
claims.claim: Only an eDiscovery Administrator can remove case members.
claims.quote: Only an eDiscovery Administrator can remove users from a case. Even if you're assigned to the eDiscovery Manager role group or initially created the case, you can't remove yourself or other members from a case unless you're also an eDiscovery Administrator.

claims.claim: Adding or removing a role from a case-member role group removes that group from its cases.
claims.quote: If you add or remove a role from a role group that you added as a member of a case, the role group is automatically removed as a member of the case (or any case the role group is a member of).

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risks and limits, Groups do not behave as expected
claims.claim: The eDiscovery Manager role group needs a mail-enabled security group, with mail-enabled security groups being the only membership option.
claims.quote: On Manage eDiscovery Manager, select Choose users or Choose groups.
claims.fix: Replace 'The eDiscovery Manager role group needs a mail-enabled security group' with 'When adding a group to the eDiscovery Managers subgroup, use a mail-enabled security group; individual users can also be assigned.' Replace 'Mail-enabled security groups only' in the row note with 'Group membership uses mail-enabled security groups; individual users are also supported. This command assigns Managers, not Administrators.'

claims.where: Risks and limits, Groups do not behave as expected
claims.claim: Exchange distribution groups and Microsoft 365 Groups are unsupported as members of the eDiscovery Managers subgroup.
claims.quote: Exchange distribution groups and Microsoft 365 Groups aren't supported. You must use a mail-enabled security group

claims.where: Risks and limits, Groups do not behave as expected
claims.claim: A mail-enabled security group cannot itself be a case member.
claims.quote: You also can't add a mail-enabled security group as a member of a case.

claims.where: Risks and limits, Holds are snapshots; What to check
claims.claim: Group membership is captured at hold creation, so later-added members are not automatically held and the group must be re-added to reflect changes.
claims.quote: Members added to the group later are not automatically placed on hold; members removed from the group remain on hold until you update or release the policy. To reflect current membership, add the group again as a data source.

claims.where: Risks and limits, Holds are snapshots
claims.claim: A new eDiscovery hold can take up to 24 hours to take effect.
claims.quote: After you create an eDiscovery hold, it might take up to 24 hours for the hold to take effect.

claims.where: Risks and limits, Holds are snapshots
claims.claim: SharePoint Recycle Bin content is not indexed.
claims.quote: The Recycle Bin in SharePoint sites isn't indexed and therefore unavailable for searching.

claims.where: Risks and limits, Holds are snapshots
claims.claim: Selecting a subsite for a hold puts the hold on its parent site instead.
claims.quote: If you select a subsite, the hold is placed on the parent SharePoint site instead.

claims.where: Risks and limits, Filters have a ceiling; What to check
claims.claim: A search has a maximum of 100 conditions including its query and all applied search permissions filters.
claims.quote: a search query can have a maximum of 100 conditions. ... The limit for the number of conditions includes the search query itself plus all search permissions filters that the user who runs the search applies.

claims.where: Risks and limits, Filters have a ceiling
claims.claim: Search permissions filters cannot limit Exchange public-folder searches.
claims.quote: You can't use search permissions filtering to limit who can search public folders in Exchange.

claims.where: controls[4].note; Risks and limits, Deleting Copilot data; What to check
claims.claim: A mailbox hold or retention policy keeps AI data that a purge attempts to delete, so the documented workflow removes those policies first.
claims.quote: Before you can delete Copilot or other AI application data from a mailbox, you have to remove any hold or retention policy that is assigned to a target mailbox. If you don't remove the hold or retention policy, the data you're trying to delete is retained.

claims.where: Risks and limits, Deleting Copilot data
claims.claim: The AI-data article documents a 10-items-per-mailbox deletion limit.
claims.quote: You can remove up to 10 items per mailbox at one time.
claims.fix: Append 'The Graph purgeData reference instead documents a maximum of 100 items per location; the two pages differ.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/security-ediscoverysearch-purgedata?view=graph-rest-1.0.

claims.where: Risks and limits, Deleting Copilot data
claims.claim: Deleting a conversation does not delete associated Copilot memory.
claims.quote: Deleting a conversation or message from Microsoft Purview or eDiscovery doesn't delete the associated Copilot memory.

claims.where: Risks and limits, Search and purge
claims.claim: Search and purge is unsupported on a mailbox with litigation hold.
claims.quote: Search and purge isn't supported if a mailbox has a litigation hold.

claims.where: Risks and limits, Required enterprise apps

claims.quote: If you don't enable these apps, you can't access all eDiscovery view, filter, and search features. These apps must be up to date and correctly configured. Make sure that Enabled for users to sign-in is selected.

claims.claim: App-only authentication for eDiscovery cmdlets in Security & Compliance PowerShell is unsupported and Microsoft advises migration to Graph.
claims.quote: App-only authentication for eDiscovery cmdlets in Security & Compliance PowerShell is unsupported. Transition automations to Microsoft Graph APIs where available.

claims.where: controls[2].ui; Open questions, search permissions filters
claims.claim: No portal creation path is documented for search permissions filters; Microsoft documents four Security & Compliance PowerShell cmdlets.
claims.quote: Searched: 'eDiscovery search permissions filtering create portal UI New-ComplianceSecurityFilter'; opened edisc-search-permission-filtering and edisc-compliance-boundaries. They describe New/Get/Set/Remove-ComplianceSecurityFilter, not a portal creation path.

claims.claim: New-ComplianceSecurityFilter -FilterName <name of filter> -Users <user or role group> -Filters <filter> creates a search permissions filter.
claims.quote: New-ComplianceSecurityFilter -FilterName <name of filter> -Users <user or role group> -Filters <filter>
claims.fix: The cited article prints this syntax, but the cmdlet reference marks Action mandatory. Use 'New-ComplianceSecurityFilter -FilterName <name of filter> -Users <user or role group> -Filters <filter> -Action All' and cite https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/new-compliancesecurityfilter?view=exchange-ps; note that All applies the filter to all search actions.

claims.claim: eDiscovery > Cases > case > Hold policies > Create policy reaches the case hold creation workflow.
claims.quote:
Select a case, and then select the Hold policies tab.
4. On the Hold policies dashboard, select Create policy.
claims.fix: Keep the path but narrow the row's governs to 'Creation of a case hold policy', consistent with the API correction. The printed path reaches policy creation, not the subsequent data-source selection.

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/security/cases/ediscoveryCases/{ediscoveryCaseId}/legalHolds sets which mailboxes and sites are preserved by a case hold.
claims.quote: Create a new ediscoveryHoldPolicy object. ... displayName | String | The display name of the legal hold policy. Required. ... contentQuery | String | KQL query that specifies content to be held in the specified locations. Optional.
claims.fix: Narrow controls[3].governs and its rendered label to 'Creation of a case hold policy'. Keep the endpoint, but make the note 'Creates the policy only; the request body requires displayName and optionally sets contentQuery. Mailboxes and sites must be added separately.' The create endpoint does not select locations; Microsoft documents separate POST legalHolds/{ediscoveryHoldPolicyId}/userSources and siteSources operations.

claims.claim: The documented automation for AI-data deletion is POST /v1.0/security/cases/ediscoveryCases/{ediscoveryCaseID}/searches/{ediscoverySearchID}/purgeData.
claims.quote: In Graph Explorer, run the following POST request to delete the items returned by the search
claims.fix: Keep the method and path. Add to the row note 'The request body uses purgeAreas to select mailboxes and purgeType to select recoverable or permanentlyDelete.' The v1.0 reference at https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/security-ediscoverysearch-purgedata?view=graph-rest-1.0 documents those properties.
